steps.notes: Passes steptest with any reasonable hbar (tolerances very loose); docstring wrongly says elements are float (targets are complex128); prompt's hbar value is typographically corrupted.

Passes 4/4 ONLY with hbar=1.0545718e-34 exactly (matches target to 1e-15). Fails 3/4 with scipy.constants.hbar or CODATA 1.054571817e-34. Algorithm/conventions otherwise fully reproducible (h=T/nstep, x0=L/2, psi0=exp(-(x-x0)^2/2sigma^2)exp(i*kappa*x), grid linspace(0,L,N+1), boundaries zeroed).

findings.evidence: The prompt's statement of the required physical constant is corrupted: both problem_description_main and step 15.1's prompt say 'the reduced Plank's constant $\hbar=\times 10^{-34} Js$' -- the mantissa is MISSING entirely. Meanwhile the frozen 15.2 targets demand that exact constant to ~10 significant digits: implementing the step with hbar=1.0545718e-34 reproduces all 3 numeric targets to max|diff| ~1e-15 and steptest gives 4/4 PASS; the identical code with scipy.constants.hbar (1.0545718176461565e-34, relative difference only 1.7e-8) gives max|diff| 4.1e-7 / 7.5e-7 / 6.9e-8 on tests 1-3 and steptest gives 3/4 FAIL (only the symmetry test 4 passes). CODATA 1.054571817e-34 also fails (max|diff| 4.0e-7/7.2e-7/6.6e-8), as do textbook 1.0546e-34 (1.2e-3), 1.05457e-34 (7.6e-5), 1.055e-34, 1.05e-34, and the literal-typo 1e-34 (0.77). The amplification mechanism: 180-1999 Crank-Nicolson steps accumulate phase ~ E*T/hbar ~ 10^2 rad, multiplying a relative hbar error by ~10^2-10^3 into the wavefunction, while np.allclose tolerance at near-zero components of the (N+1,) real-part output is just atol=1e-8. Net effect: a competent solver passes iff they happen to write hbar as the 8-digit truncation '1.0545718e-34'; the physically most accurate choices (scipy.constants.hbar, CODATA) are scored WRONG on 3 of 4 tests. Repro files: review/work/15/impl_gold_hbar.py (4/4 pass) vs review/work/15/impl_scipy_hbar.py (1/4 pass); the only difference is the hbar literal.
findings.suggested_fix: Two-part fix: (1) repair the prompt text in problem_description_main and step 15.1 to state the constant explicitly as 'hbar = 1.0545718e-34 J s' (the value the targets encode); (2) loosen the 15.2 test tolerance to cover legitimate constant roundings, e.g. assert np.allclose(result, target, atol=1e-5) or rtol=1e-3 with atol=2e-6 -- correct CODATA-based solutions differ by <8e-7 and would pass, while structurally wrong solutions differ by >1e-3.

findings.evidence: The diagonal entries of the targets are 1 + O(1e-7)*i, so np.allclose's rtol*|target| ~ 1e-5 makes the imaginary part of the diagonals essentially unconstrained, and the off-diagonal targets (~4.6e-8) sit at the atol=1e-8 floor, allowing ~20% error. Verified wrong implementations that PASS all 3 of 15.1's tests: (a) diagonal signs swapped (a1 = 1-2hC, b1 = 1+2hC -- a real conceptual error that inverts the CN scheme); (b) purely real diagonals (a1 = b1 = 1, imaginary part dropped entirely); (c) hbar = 1e-34 (the prompt's literal typo, 5% wrong); (d) hbar = 1.2e-34 (+14% wrong). Only gross structural errors fail (off-diagonals zeroed or sign-swapped, factor-2 error in C). Also note test 1 uses N=2, producing 1x1 matrices where even A=B=[[1.0]] passes that test. So step 15.1 awards credit to implementations whose A/B matrices are physically wrong, while step 15.2 simultaneously demands 10-significant-digit precision -- the two steps' tolerance regimes are wildly inconsistent.
findings.suggested_fix: Strengthen 15.1's tests: compare A and B against targets with explicit tight tolerance scaled to the entries, e.g. assert np.allclose(init_AB(...), target, rtol=1e-6, atol=1e-12), and/or add a test with larger h (e.g. h=1e-15) so the imaginary parts are O(1e-5)-O(1) and no longer hide below rtol*|diagonal|.

findings.evidence: function_header docstring says 'A,B: A and B matrices; 2D arrays of dimension N-1 by N-1 where each element is a float', but the matrix entries are necessarily complex (background gives C = i*hbar/(4*m*a^2), a1 = 1+2hC etc.), and the frozen h5 targets are dtype complex128 (e.g. 15.1 test 1 diagonal 1+9.26e-08j). A solver who takes the docstring literally and returns float (real-part) matrices fails test 2 (off-diagonals 4.6e-8j vs 0 exceeds atol 1e-8), though it passes test 1 (1x1 case).
findings.suggested_fix: Change the docstring to 'where each element is a complex number' (and similarly any 'float' claims about A/B elsewhere).

overall_assessment: The physics, signatures, and conventions of both steps are fully reproducible (gold pipeline recovered to machine precision: h=T/nstep, x grid linspace(0,L,N+1), x0=L/2, unnormalized Gaussian, zeroed boundaries), but the problem mis-scores in both directions. Step 15.1's tests are so loose that conceptually wrong matrices (sign-swapped or real diagonals, hbar wrong by 14%) pass, while step 15.2 fails any solver who does not write hbar as exactly '1.0545718e-34' -- including those using scipy.constants.hbar or the CODATA value -- because the prompt's stated constant is typographically corrupted ('$\hbar=\times 10^{-34} Js$', mantissa missing) and 1999 CN steps amplify the 8th-digit discrepancy past the default allclose tolerance. As-is, 15.2's score is a lottery on the solver's textual form of hbar; fixing the prompt typo and/or loosening 15.2's tolerance makes the problem fair.
